source: A clean B1 turn on g4.4 «Le lendemain» (the page of page-b1-clean-le-lendemain), French screen. Written for this fixture.

learner.grammatical_gender_note: Do not gender the learner: no gendered adjective, participle or endearment about them, no gendered pronoun for them, and never an inclusive-dot form such as trempé·e. Use natural neutral phrasing in EVERY field, including the chapter title and question, narration, dialogue and suggested response. For example: 'Tu as pris la pluie', 'Tu veux entrer ?', 'Ça te plaît', 'Tu peux venir ?'. Do not solve gender agreement by joining masculine and feminine endings.
learner.register_note: Address the learner as «tu» (ton/ta/tes; e.g. «Tu as …») in every sentence that is not a character's own line. Never «vous, votre, vos» for the learner.

cast.name: Mme Diallo
cast.role: Minor character: the baker on the corner, in her fifties, floured apron, reading glasses on a chain.
cast.personality: Brisk and kind. Running line: «Une tradition pas trop cuite, c'est ça ?»
cast.wants: Her regulars, and Le Mistral next door.
cast.speech_pattern: «Une tradition pas trop cuite, c'est ça ?» «Et demain ?»
cast.dynamic_with_user: Knows the learner's face from gap 1.

scene.premise_fr: Lundi matin, à la boulangerie de Mme Diallo. La file d'attente sort jusque sur le trottoir.
scene.objective_native: Mme Diallo veut savoir comment tu vas depuis samedi.
scene.objective_semantics: And you, how are you holding up after Saturday? Met when the learner's words answer it, in any direction.
scene.opening_line_fr: Et vous, ça va depuis samedi ?
scene.suggested_response_fr: Ça va mieux, merci. Le croissant aide beaucoup.

panels.visual_direction: Close on Mme Diallo's hands slipping a croissant into the paper bag.

dialogue.text_fr: Et un croissant. Pour Odile. Elle en prenait toujours un le lundi.

payload.rubric: Grade only what the task asks; any honest answer counts.
payload.learner_text: Ça va mieux, merci. Mais tout le monde me regarde un peu bizarrement depuis la fête.

content.reply_fr: Ils regardent, oui. Ils ont vu la photo au mur, et ils ne savent pas encore quoi dire. Laissez-leur une semaine. Et demain ?
content.understood_intent: The learner is better but feels watched since the party.
